newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S BALKAN RESUMES FLIGHTS FROM THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S BALKAN RESUMES FLIGHTS FROM THURSDAY.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-run Balkan Airlines said it would resume international flights on Thursday after cancelling departures for 24 hours because of strike threats by technical staff.
Airline spokesman Viktor Melamed said an agreement had been reached on Wednesday for protests to be shelved for 10 days while negotiations were carried out.
"Balkan will run tomorrow 22 flights which will include the 16 flights postponed from today," Melamed said. He said another 14 aircraft arrivals were scheduled.
On Tuesday, the board of directors decided to postpone flights, saying they could not be sure whether aircraft would be properly checked.
The airline's management and technical staff signed a protocol on Monday agreeing monthly negotiations on payments to compensate for soaring inflation, an airline statement said.
But technical staff said on Tuesday they disagreed with the scheme and threatened individual protests including work stoppages.
Officials said the airline incurred losses of $50 million last year due to leasing fees, the drastic fall of the lev against the dollar and penalties on overdue payments.
The airline's new management said earlier this year that Balkan needed a complete restructuring to stabilise the company and make it profitable and attractive for potential foreign investors.
